title: Describe a sequence of transformations that shows two figures are similar

sections.skill: Describe a sequence of transformations that shows two figures are similar

questions.skill: Describe a sequence of transformations that shows two figures are similar
questions.prompt: Describe a sequence of transformations that maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF.
questions.prompt_markup: Describe a sequence of transformations that maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF.
questions.correct_answer: A dilation with a scale factor of 2 and the origin as the center, followed by a 180° rotation about the origin.
questions.grading_note: Any correct sequence is accepted, for example the rotation first, then the dilation.

questions.skill: Describe a sequence of transformations that shows two figures are similar
questions.prompt: Explain why a 2-by-3 rectangle and a 4-by-6 rectangle are similar.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why a 2-by-3 rectangle and a 4-by-6 rectangle are similar.
questions.correct_answer: A dilation with a scale factor of 2 (followed by rigid motions to move it into place) maps the first rectangle onto the second.

questions.prompt_markup: Which sequence of transformations maps a figure onto a figure that is similar but not congruent?

choices.text: A dilation with a scale factor of 3, then a translation

questions.correct_answer: A dilation with a scale factor of 3, then a translation

questions.skill: Describe a sequence of transformations that shows two figures are similar
questions.prompt: Are a 3-4-5 triangle and a 5-12-13 triangle similar? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup: Are a 3-4-5 triangle and a 5-12-13 triangle similar? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: No. The ratios of corresponding sides (3/5, 4/12, 5/13) are not equal, so no dilation and rigid motions can map one onto the other.

sections.skill: Use a translation and a dilation to show that any two circles are similar

questions.skill: Use a translation and a dilation to show that any two circles are similar
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Circle A has center (0, 0) and radius 2. Circle B has center (5, 1) and radius 6. Describe a translation followed by a dilation that maps circle A onto circle B.
questions.prompt_markup:
Circle A has center (0, 0) and radius 2. Circle B has center (5, 1) and radius 6.
Describe a translation followed by a dilation that maps circle A onto circle B.
questions.correct_answer: Translate 5 units right and 1 unit up, then dilate about (5, 1) with a scale factor of 3.
questions.grading_note: Any correct sequence is accepted, for example a dilation about (0, 0) with scale factor 3 followed by a translation 5 units right and 1 unit up.

questions.prompt: Which statement explains why any two circles are similar?

choices.text: A rotation alone maps any circle onto any other circle.
All circles have the same radius.
A translation moves one center onto the other, and then a dilation about that center makes the radii equal.
All circles have the same area.

questions.correct_answer: A translation moves one center onto the other, and then a dilation about that center makes the radii equal.
